1.m: Consciousness is the self.
[Contracted] knowledge is bondage.
The group of origins [and] the body of limited parts [are bondage].
The basis of [such] knowledge is Mātṛkā.
Zealous effort is Bhairava.
Through union with the wheel of energies comes the dissolution of the universe.
Amidst the division of waking, dream, and deep sleep, the experience of the fourth [state] emerges.
Waking is [common] knowledge.
Dream is conceptual thought.
Deep sleep is non-discrimination [and] Māyā.
The enjoyer of the triad is the lord of heroes.
The stages of yoga are wonder.
The power of will is Umā, the maiden.
The visible [universe] is the body.
From the union of the mind in the heart, there is perception of the visible and of the void.
Or, from contemplation on the pure principle, [arises] the power of non-bondage.
Reflective discernment is the knowledge of the self.
The bliss of the world is the joy of absorption.
In union with Śakti, [there is] the production of a body.
[He gains] the joining of elements, the separation of elements, and the conjunction of the universe.
From the arising of pure knowledge comes mastery over the wheel [of energies].
From contemplation of the great lake comes the experience of the potency of mantra.

2.m: The reality of the body of knowledge is the secret of mantra.
The expansion of the mind in the womb is the dream of undifferentiated knowledge.
Upon the spontaneous emergence of knowledge, [there is] the state of Śiva, Khecarī.
[The means is] the awakening of the wheel of Mātṛkā.
Upon the dissolution of knowledge, [there is] the appearance of dream arising from it.

3.m: The self is the mind.
[Contracted] knowledge is bondage.
Māyā is the non-discrimination among principles such as Kalā.
In the body is the dissolution of the parts.
[He attains] the dissolution of the channels, the conquest of elements, isolation from elements, and separation of elements.
Attainment [arises] through the veil of delusion.
From the conquest of delusion and from boundless extension, [comes] the conquest of innate knowledge.
[The yogin] makes waking an auxiliary ray.
The self is the dancer.
The inner self is the stage.
The senses are the spectators.
Through the power of intelligence comes the attainment of pure being.
The state of autonomy is established.
As there, so elsewhere.
[The practice is] attention to the seed.
Established in the posture, he easily plunges into the lake.
He accomplishes the fashioning [of the world] according to his own measure.
When knowledge does not perish, rebirth perishes.
Presiding over the guttural group and others are Māheśvarī and the rest, the mothers of bound souls.
The fourth [state] should be poured into the three like oil.
Immersed, he should enter with his own mind.
When the vital breath moves evenly, there is equal vision.
In the middle, an inferior emission [occurs].
Through joining one's apprehension to the objects, what was lost rises again.
He becomes equal to Śiva.
The subsistence of the body is his religious vow.
[His] conversation is recitation.
[His] gift is self-knowledge.
He who is established in the powers of awareness is also the cause of wisdom.
The universe is the unfolding of his own power.
[So too are its] maintenance and dissolution.
Even while those [states] proceed, there is no rupture, because of his state as the knower.
[His] regarding pleasure and pain is external.
One freed from them is solitary.
One bound by delusion, however, consists of action.
When duality is dissolved, [there is] the capacity to create another world.
The power of the senses [arises] from one's own experience.
[Then occurs] the enlivening of the three states and the rest.
Just as with the state of consciousness, so it is with the body, the senses, and external objects.
Through desire, the transported soul moves outward.
For one whose awareness is mounted upon That, with the destruction of that [desire], the limited soul ceases to be.

3.s: bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ
3.d: भूतकञ्चुकी तदा विमुक्तो भूयः पतिसमः परः
3.m: [Though still] cloaked in the elements, he is then liberated, supreme, again equal to the Lord.
The connection with the vital breath is natural.
By constraint upon the inner center of the nose, what [need is there] here for the left, the right, and the central channels?
May there be re-integration [into the divine reality] again.
